question_en: An otherwise normal distribution has a skewness of −0.77. Regarding the distribution's measures of central tendency, it is most likely that its:
option_a: mean is larger than its mode.
option_b: median is larger than its mean.
option_c: median is larger than its mode.
explanation_en:
Skewness measures the symmetry of a distribution. A normal distribution is perfectly symmetric and has the same likelihood of values at a given
standard deviation on both sides of the mean. Skewed distributions are asymmetric and have more extreme values in the direction of the
skew.
Due to the frequency of extreme results, skewness also impacts a distribution's measures of central tendency differently. For a unimodal
distribution:
the median will be pulled toward the direction of the skew more than the mode, and
the mean will be pulled toward the direction of the skew more than the median.
In this question, the distribution has a skew of −0.77 (ie, negatively skewed), indicating small but more frequent values in the right tail and a few
extreme values in the left tail. This pulls the mean farther to the left than the median, and therefore the median is larger than the mean.
(Choices A and C) A positively skewed distribution has a mean that is larger than its median, which is larger than its mode.

question_en: .A one-week sample of daily closing net asset values for a fund is randomly selected. The observations for the week were 38, 41, 35, 51, and 45. The mean absolute deviation (MAD) for this sample is closest to:
explanation_en:
Mean absolute deviation (MAD) measures dispersion (ie, variability) of observations around the mean. Dispersion refers to the difference
between an observation and the mean. Higher dispersion means that the observations are more spread out around the mean, which indicates a
greater probability of observations that are significantly higher or lower than the mean. In finance, dispersion indicates risk.
Since the sum of all dispersions around the mean equals 0, MAD instead uses the absolute value of each dispersion. The sum of all the absolute
values is divided by the number of observations, which produces the average dispersion. The calculations are shown below:
(Choice A) Data in a sample will be both above and below the mean, so some dispersions around the mean are negative and others are
positive. The sum of all dispersions equals 0, so the average also equals 0. By using the absolute value of the dispersions, MAD always
generates a number ≥ 0.
(Choice C) 6.0 results from dividing the sum of the absolute values by (n − 1), or 4, instead of 5. The number of observations minus 1 is used
only when calculating the standard deviation of a sample. MAD uses the actual number of observations.

explanation_en:

question_en: For four years, an investor invests €1,000,000 annually in a stock at the following prices (per share): The average price per share paid for the stock over the four-year period is closest to:
explanation_en:
The harmonic mean is a weighted average. It is a measure of central tendency typically used for averaging ratios (stated as "amount per unit")
where an observation's value is inversely proportional to its weight in the average. It can be used for cost averaging (ie, finding average price per
share) when fixed amounts are invested periodically.
In this instance, since the investor is investing annually the same total amount, €1,000,000, a lower stock price implies that a larger number of
shares can be purchased. Thus, the lower (higher) share prices should be assigned larger (smaller) weights in the average since a greater
(smaller) number of shares in the investment portfolio was purchased at that price. The harmonic mean assigns a larger weight to smaller
observations and therefore is appropriate.
(Choice B) The geometric mean is most appropriate for calculating the average growth rate over multiple consecutive return periods by taking
compounding into account. It is not a weighted average.
(Choice C) The arithmetic mean is a simple average of the purchase prices, assigning equal weight to all observations.

question_en:
A distribution of sample stock returns has the following statistics:

|   |   |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic mean | 0.45 |
| Standard deviation | 0.67 |
| Skewness | 0.0 |
| Excess kurtosis | 0.83 |

Compared with a normal distribution, this distribution will most likely have extreme returns that occur:
explanation_en:
Kurtosis measures the proportion of values in a distribution that are large deviations from the mean. For investors, large deviations from the
mean return tend to indicate higher risk, so greater kurtosis indicates riskier investments.
A normal distribution has kurtosis of 3 (ie, a mesokurtic distribution). Excess kurtosis is measured as kurtosis − 3. A normal distribution will have 0
excess kurtosis:
Positive excess kurtosis (ie, a leptokurtic distribution) indicates that there is a greater proportion of extreme values than in a normal
distribution; therefore, the tails of the distribution are fatter.
Negative excess kurtosis (ie, a platykurtic distribution) indicates that there is a smaller proportion of extreme values than in a normal
distribution; therefore, the tails of the distribution are thinner.
In this scenario, the excess kurtosis is 0.83. Since the value is positive, the tails of the distribution will be fatter than in a normal distribution.
Therefore, this distribution is more likely to have extreme returns than a normal distribution (Choices A and B).

question_en: When conducting correlation analysis, the most appropriate approach is to exclude:
option_c: only outliers that are generated from noise.
explanation_en:
Correlation analysis indicates the direction and strength of the linear relationship between two variables. However, correlation analysis has
limitations that can reduce its reliability as a summary statistic. These limitations include the following:
Outliers have significant impact. Outliers can create significant changes to the correlation between two variables. Analysts must judge
whether outliers contain information about the relationship between the variables and should therefore remain in the dataset or are noise
and should be excluded from the dataset (Choices A and B). If outliers from noise remain, they will reduce the correlation metric's
reliability.
Correlation measures only linear relationships. Variables can have a strong nonlinear (eg, logarithmic) relationship while also having
low correlation values since correlation does not account for a nonlinear relationship.
High correlation coefficients can be caused by spurious (ie, false) correlation. This occurs when:
the correlation is due to chance and not to a meaningful relationship.
calculations combine the two variables with a third variable.
the correlation results from a direct relationship to a third variable.

question_en: An otherwise normal distribution with a mean of 0 has an excess kurtosis of −0.6. Which of the following best describes the distribution?
option_a: Its mean will be smaller than its median
option_b: Its tails will be thinner than a normal distribution
option_c: It is more likely to have negative values than positive values
explanation_en:
Kurtosis measures the proportion of outcomes in a distribution's "tails." A normal distribution has total kurtosis of 3 and excess kurtosis of 0
(ie, the normal distribution is mesokurtic). A distribution with negative excess kurtosis (ie, a platykurtic distribution) will have:
thinner tails, indicating a smaller proportion of extreme values, and
a lower peak, indicating fewer results clustered around the mean.
In this scenario, the distribution is otherwise normal except that it has excess kurtosis of −0.6. This indicates that the distribution is platykurtic, and
thus that its tails will be thinner than the tails of a normal distribution.
(Choice A) Kurtosis does not affect the symmetry, and therefore the location of the measures of central tendency, of an otherwise normal
distribution. A normal distribution's mean is equal to its median.
(Choice C) Kurtosis does not affect the symmetry of an otherwise normal distribution. Since the mean of the distribution is 0 and the distribution
remains symmetric, the distribution of positive values is the same as the distribution of negative values.

question_en: Assuming assets have a unimodal return distribution, which of the following assets would be most appropriate for an investor aiming to maximize mean returns? An asset with an expected return distribution that is:
explanation_en:
Investors commonly consider the level of symmetry in a return distribution. For unimodal distributions, if the return distribution is perfectly
symmetrical, where the arithmetic mean, median, and mode are equal, then the probability of a gain is the same as the probability of a loss.
Skewness refers to the lack of symmetry in a distribution.
A positively skewed return distribution has a long right tail with:
fewer but large returns above the mean and
frequent but smaller returns below the mean.
These large returns pull the mean to the right of the mode and the median, so the mean is greater than the median, which is greater than the
mode. Positively skewed returns are most appropriate for the investor aiming to maximize mean returns since the mean expected return is
greater than for assets with symmetrical or negatively skewed distributions, all else equal (Choices A and C).
If a return distribution is negatively skewed, it has a long left tail: fewer but larger returns below the mean with frequent but smaller returns above
the mean. The mean is less than the median, which is less than the mode, and the mean expected return is less than that for a symmetrical or
positively skewed unimodal distribution.

question_en:
The correlation of three portfolios' daily stock returns over the past decade is presented in the following matrix:

|   | Portfolio 1 | Portfolio 2 | Portfolio 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Portfolio 1 | 1.00 | 0.83 | −0.77 |
| Portfolio 2 |  | 1.00 | 0.13 |
| Portfolio 3 |  |  | 1.00 |

Based on only this information, which two portfolios most likely demonstrated the weakest linear relationship?
explanation_en:
Correlation measures the linear relationship between two variables. When the relationship is direct (ie, the variables generally move in the
same direction), correlation will be positive. When the relationship is inverse (ie, the variables generally move in opposite directions), correlation
will be negative.
Correlation is a standardized measure that indicates both the direction and strength of a linear relationship. A correlation value closer to 0
suggests a weak linear relationship between the variables. If the value moves closer to either −1 or 1 (ie, away from 0), it indicates a stronger
relationship. A value of −1 indicates a perfect negative linear relationship; a value of 1 indicates a perfect positive linear relationship.
In this scenario, the weakest linear relationship is between Portfolios 2 and 3 because their correlation of 0.13 is the closest to 0. Note: The
correlation between any variable and itself will always be 1.
(Choice A) Portfolios 1 and 2 have a correlation of 0.83, indicating a strong positive linear relationship.
(Choice B) Portfolios 1 and 3 have a correlation of −0.77, indicating a strong negative linear relationship.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\1. Quantitative Methods\1.03 Statistical Measures of Asset Returns - Answers.pdf
question_en: If a unimodal distribution has a skewness of 0.8, which of the following measures of central tendency is the greatest?
explanation_en:
Skewness measures how nonsymmetrical a distribution is. Skewed distributions typically have more extreme values in one tail and more
moderate values in the other. As a distribution becomes more skewed and either the left or right tail grows higher or longer, the values farther from
the middle of the distribution are more likely to pull the arithmetic mean (simple mean or average) away from the distribution center than the
median or mode. Because the arithmetic mean weights every value equally, it is more heavily influenced by outliers and extreme data points.
A normal distribution, which is symmetrical, has a skewness of 0. A distribution with a skewness of 0.8 is positive, suggesting that there is a larger
number of higher-valued data points. Since the tail to the right is longer in a distribution with positive skewness, the arithmetic mean is more
affected than the median and mode.
(Choice A) The mode (most common value) normally is least affected by skewness in a unimodal distribution. The presence of skewness in a
distribution suggests a lack of symmetry (ie, one of the tails is higher or longer than the other). Altering the size of a distribution's tails typically will
not change the most frequent data point.
(Choice B) The median (middle value) is normally more affected than the mode by skewness in a unimodal distribution, although less affected
than the arithmetic mean. In a positively skewed distribution, the greater number of larger values will pull the median to the right. Although the
median is affected by the values in the right tail, the arithmetic mean is more affected by the larger values.
